test.name: Luxembourg indexing quirk: civil birth acts index children by given name only — drop surname, re-anchor on parent names
test.description: Executing pli_001 (find Theresia Reding's 1846 civil birth in Arsdorf, Luxembourg), a surname-anchored search returns records where a Reding is named as a PARENT, not as the child (record-search-reding-surname-not-found) — three mother-side hits, none of which is Theresia's own birth. Luxembourg civil birth acts index the newborn by given name only; the child carries no indexed surname. The skill must recognize this indexing pattern and drop surname, re-anchoring on givenName=Theresia + fatherSurname=Reding (or fatherGivenName=Jakob, or the mother's equivalents), anchored on recordCountry=Luxembourg, which surfaces the birth (record-search-theresia-luxembourg-hit, ark 6LYM-X1PN). Guards the Luxembourg name-only doctrine: a surname-nil in this collection is NOT evidence the birth is unindexed.

judge_context: CORE (Tool Arguments): the birth search must NOT keep 'Reding' as the surname constraint. Luxembourg civil birth acts index the newborn by given name only — there is no indexed surname on the child. A query with surname=Reding returns records where Reding is a parent, not the child, and this collection returns 3 such parent-side hits (record-search-reding-surname-not-found). Score Tool Arguments 3 if a record_search drops the surname and searches instead with givenName=Theresia plus a parent anchor (fatherSurname=Reding, fatherGivenName=Jakob, motherSurname=Schroeder, or similar) anchored on recordCountry=Luxembourg or collectionId=5000012. Score 1 if the skill keeps surname=Reding as the only anchor and does not re-anchor on the parents.

CORE (Correctness): the skill should recognize that Luxembourg civil birth acts index children by given name only, and re-anchor on the given name plus the parents' names already in the subject record (father: Jakob Reding, mother: Maria Schroeder). Reaching the birth (record-search-theresia-luxembourg-hit, ark 6LYM-X1PN, born 17 June 1846, Arsdorf, daughter of Jakob Reding and Maria Schroeder) is the successful outcome.

If the skill receives the 3 parent-side hits from the surname search (record-search-reding-surname-not-found) and concludes 'birth not found' or 'Theresia is unindexed' without also trying a parent-anchored, no-surname search, that is a FAIL. The surname-nil from a Luxembourg civil birth collection says nothing about whether the child's birth is indexed.

Completeness: the search should be logged (the initial surname attempt and/or the successful parent-anchored attempt). Finding the birth (6LYM-X1PN) is a complete answer; do NOT require the skill to also complete extraction in this test.

Do NOT penalize the skill for not calling place_search or collections_search — recordCountry 'Luxembourg' is a sufficient anchor for the civil birth search, and a validate_research_schema call is acceptable if made.

record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. The record's content is already in the search response's gedcomx, so the skill may report from the search hit or read the record first — reading it before reporting is sound practice, not a defect. Score neither path down.
